hero.pitch: An aerospace engineer turned developer, I have spent the last {years} years building business applications in Angular and Java for major French public-sector bodies: first the Ministry of the Armed Forces, then the Directorate-General for Maritime Affairs, Fisheries and Aquaculture (DGAMPA). I work in heavily regulated domains, where a business rule translated badly has concrete consequences and where code quality is judged over the long run.

profileIntro.heading: An engineer turned developer
profileIntro.paragraph1: After graduating as an aerospace engineer from ISAE-ENSMA in 2021, I chose to retrain as a software developer. Turbines were an interesting subject, but the job leaned towards highly theoretical calculations aimed at optimising a fraction of a percent of a sub-assembly of an aircraft engine. Looking for work with more tangible results, professionally and personally, I retrained through a Java conversion programme that came with a permanent contract at Sopra Steria. I passed the Java certification at the end of that training, in July 2021.
profileIntro.paragraph2: Since then, 4 assignments on business applications under strong regulatory constraints. At Sopra Steria, for the Ministry of the Armed Forces, I spent a year and a half on data migration (Talend, Java, SQL), loading various source files into the database of a military aircraft maintenance web application, then 2 years of Angular and Java development on another maintenance application, this time for ground vehicles. At Capgemini, I took over the pleasure-craft management applications of the Directorate-General for Maritime Affairs, Fisheries and Aquaculture (DGAMPA), in Angular and Java, and built the 2026 taxation scheme end to end. Today at Open, still for the DGAMPA, I am leading the rebuild of the aquaculture land registry management application, in Angular and Java, based on the French State Design System and compliant with the RGAA accessibility standard.
profileIntro.paragraph3: Beyond that Angular/Java stack, it is above all the scope of my role that has widened: frontend referent, leading a team of 2 developers against client milestones, mentoring an intern and then an apprentice. That role changed the way I work: I now spend as much time unblocking, reviewing and explaining as writing code, and that is what moves the team forward.
profileIntro.paragraph4: AI is now part of my daily toolkit (exploring an approach, generating a skeleton, reviewing a diff), with targeted prompts and minimal context to keep the token cost under control. Not a single line ships without being reviewed, understood and owned. In parallel, I have designed and deployed several applications on my own, including Life Rise, which brings together 19 modules, a conversational assistant and sharing between profiles: my testing ground for new Angular features before proposing them on an assignment.

skills.honestyBody: The percentages above are a self-assessment, not an exam grade. They reflect how far I can go on a given subject on my own. Above 85, I am autonomous and can make calls for the team. Between 70 and 85, I deliver without difficulty but I am still learning. Below that, I have practised in a real setting without making it my speciality.
